findings.summary: Mohammed Asaria career path: Cambridge law -> Hogan Lovells (2001-06) -> HSBC Dubai (2006-07) -> Rasameel Investment Bank Kuwait (2008-10) -> founded Range Developments (2011)
findings.detail: Mohammed Asaria: Trinity College Cambridge law degree (1997-2000). Career: Hogan Lovells (fka Lovells) City of London solicitor (Sep 2001-Aug 2006), HSBC Dubai Associate Director investment banking (Aug 2006-Dec 2007), Rasameel Investment Bank Kuwait Managing Director (Jan 2008-Sep 2010). Founded Range Developments 2011/2012. Currently Founder, Managing Director and Board Member. Dubai-based. The Rasameel connection is notable — Rasameel is a Kuwaiti investment company regulated by Capital Markets Authority of Kuwait, with pillars in wealth management, asset management, and alternative investments. The progression from Kuwaiti investment banking to founding a CBI resort developer suggests Gulf capital networks as likely Range funding sources. Not found on OpenSanctions or LittleSis as individual.

findings.summary: Asaria career: Cambridge law -> Hogan Lovells -> HSBC Dubai -> Rasameel Kuwait -> Range Developments 2011 — prior HSBC and Middle East banking experience relevant to CBI fund channeling
findings.detail: Mohammed Asaria graduated Trinity College, Cambridge (law), then worked at Hogan Lovells (solicitor) and HSBC in London/Tokyo/Dubai, followed by Rasameel Investment Bank in Kuwait. Founded Range Developments in 2011/2012. His HSBC experience (including Dubai) is particularly relevant: HSBC's Swiss private bank (HSBC Private Bank Suisse SA, Geneva) was the institution where 28 Dominican passport holders had $40.9 million in accounts per the 2015 Swiss Leaks. While no direct link is proven between Asaria and the HSBC Swiss accounts, his HSBC tenure combined with the 'Bank of Dominica account in Geneva' allegation creates a circumstantial pattern worth investigating. Range is now registered in Dominica (Range Capital Partners (Dominica) Limited, Roseau) and Dubai (Boulevard Plaza, Tower 2, Office 1104).

findings.summary: Asaria's career path: Rasameel Investment Bank Kuwait (Islamic finance, MD) to Range Developments (Dubai-HQ CBI developer) — Kuwait/Gulf capital backing for Caribbean passport sales
findings.detail: Mohammed Asaria served as Managing Director at Rasameel Investment Company, a Kuwait-based Islamic Sharia-compliant investment firm regulated by Kuwait CMA. He then founded Range Developments, headquartered in Dubai, which developed CBI-funded luxury resorts in Dominica and St Kitts. Range raised USD 195M from 800 family passports for the Dominica Kempinski project. Zampolli's lawsuit alleged Asaria and Shehada sold passports to Iran/Yemen/Sudan nationals to circumvent sanctions. The Rasameel-Range pipeline represents Gulf capital backing Caribbean CBI programs that were exploited for Iranian sanctions evasion.
